rules.name: Lattice meet-join rule
rules.input_form: ordered pair of lattice elements
preconditions: A lattice order is fixed
rules.operation: Use meet and join as greatest lower and least upper bound operations.
examples: Divisibility on integers produces meet and join behavior through gcd and lcm in the appropriate positive setting
counterexamples: A partially ordered set with missing pairwise bounds is not automatically a lattice

rules.name: Universal algebra homomorphism seed
rules.input_form: map between algebras in a common signature
preconditions: A common operation signature is fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a homomorphism by preservation of each fundamental operation.
examples: Structural maps in universal algebra are defined by operation preservation rather than by set-theoretic behavior alone
counterexamples: Preserving only one selected operation in a many-operation signature is insufficient in general

rules.name: Prime ideal quotient seed
rules.input_form: commutative ring R and prime ideal p
preconditions: R is commutative and p is prime
rules.operation: Pass from a ring to an integral-domain quotient through a prime ideal.
examples: Prime ideals encode domain-like quotient behavior in commutative algebra
counterexamples: Replacing prime by arbitrary ideal is invalid in general

rules.name: Exact sequence seed
rules.input_form: composable algebraic morphisms
preconditions: Kernels and images are defined in the active category
rules.operation: Require image-equals-kernel compatibility at a stage of a sequence.
examples: Exactness measures how algebraic information passes with no gap and no excess at each stage
counterexamples: Mere composability of maps is insufficient for exactness

rules.name: Representation action seed
rules.input_form: group or algebra acting on a vector space
preconditions: A vector space and action-compatible algebraic structure are fixed
rules.operation: Model symmetry by linear transformations on a vector space.
examples: Abstract symmetry becomes matrix or operator action through representation data
counterexamples: Assigning arbitrary nonlinear self-maps does not define a linear representation

rules.name: Lie bracket axiom seed
rules.input_form: bilinear bracket operation
rules.output_form: Lie-algebra structure when alternating and Jacobi conditions hold
preconditions: A vector space and bilinear bracket are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a Lie algebra through bracket axioms.
examples: Commutators of linear operators produce a standard Lie bracket
counterexamples: Any bilinear product lacking Jacobi behavior is not automatically a Lie bracket

rules.name: Grothendieck completion seed
rules.input_form: commutative additive monoid of classes
preconditions: A commutative additive monoid of equivalence classes is fixed
rules.operation: Formally adjoin inverses to pass from a monoid of classes to a Grothendieck group.
examples: Vector-bundle isomorphism classes can be group-completed to encode stable difference data
counterexamples: Treating a monoid as already a group without formal inverses is invalid

rules.name: Distributive lattice seed
rules.input_form: lattice with candidate distributive identities
preconditions: Meet and join operations are fixed
rules.operation: Impose distributive interaction between meet and join operations.
examples: Boolean-style lattice behavior is stronger than arbitrary lattice structure and supports sharper normal forms
counterexamples: An arbitrary lattice need not satisfy distributive laws

rules.name: Congruence quotient seed
rules.input_form: algebra with a congruence relation
preconditions: An operation-preserving congruence relation is fixed
rules.operation: Construct quotient algebras from congruence relations compatible with every basic operation.
examples: Quotient construction in universal algebra depends on compatibility with the full operation signature, not just set partitioning
counterexamples: An arbitrary equivalence relation with no operation compatibility is invalid as a congruence quotient source

rules.name: Noetherian ACC seed
rules.input_form: commutative ring with ideal structure
preconditions: A commutative ring and its ideals are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize Noetherian behavior through ascending-chain stabilization or finite ideal generation.
examples: Finite generation controls ideal growth and underpins localization and algebraic-geometry constructions
counterexamples: Allowing infinite strictly ascending ideal chains violates Noetherian behavior

rules.name: Localization seed
rules.input_form: ring or module with multiplicative set
rules.output_form: localized object with selected inverses adjoined
preconditions: A multiplicative subset and compatible localization setting are fixed
rules.operation: Invert a chosen multiplicative set to focus algebraic behavior locally.
examples: Local algebra extracts behavior near primes by selectively adjoining inverses rather than globally changing every element
counterexamples: Trying to invert elements containing zero divisors or forbidden denominators without the required multiplicative-set conditions is invalid

rules.name: Projective resolution seed
rules.input_form: algebraic object in an abelian or module-like category
rules.output_form: exact chain complex of projective objects resolving it
preconditions: Projective objects and exactness are defined in the active category
rules.operation: Replace an object by an exact projective chain complex suitable for derived computations.
examples: Derived invariants are computed by resolving objects into exact chains with tractable homological pieces
counterexamples: Any chain complex is not automatically a projective resolution without exactness and projectivity hypotheses

rules.name: Ext functor seed
rules.input_form: pair of algebraic objects with a chosen resolution
preconditions: A resolution-based derived-functor setting is fixed
rules.operation: Measure higher extension data through derived Hom constructions.
examples: Higher extension classes detect information invisible to plain homomorphism spaces
counterexamples: Computing only ordinary Hom data does not automatically determine higher Ext structure

rules.name: Semisimple representation seed
rules.input_form: representation with invariant substructure decomposition data
preconditions: A representation and irreducibility notion are fixed
rules.operation: Split a semisimple representation into irreducible summands.
examples: Reducible symmetry action can still be fully understood when it splits cleanly into irreducible blocks
counterexamples: A reducible representation with nontrivial extension data need not be semisimple

rules.name: Lie group bridge seed
rules.input_form: smooth Lie group with identity tangent data
rules.output_form: associated Lie algebra and infinitesimal structure
preconditions: A smooth Lie group and tangent-space bracket construction are fixed
rules.operation: Pass from local smooth group structure to its tangent Lie algebra.
examples: Continuous symmetry can be studied locally by brackets on tangent-space generators rather than only by global multiplication laws
counterexamples: An arbitrary topological group without the required smooth structure is not automatically a Lie-group/Lie-algebra bridge case

rules.name: K0 additivity seed
rules.input_form: short exact sequence of admissible classes or objects
preconditions: A K0-type class construction and exact-sequence setting are fixed
rules.operation: Impose additivity of K0 classes across short exact sequences.
examples: Exact decompositions contribute stable class relations even when objects are not literally equal componentwise
counterexamples: Ignoring exact-sequence structure loses the additive meaning of K0 classes

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion

preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
